notes: §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR9: "The NO REWIND and REVERSED phrases must only be used with" sequential single reel/unit files and "Sequential files wholly contained within a single reel of tape within a multiple file tape environment." The rule restricts the program; the part the source text decides is the organization, and BindOpen enforces it through CheckOpenTapePhrase over the two OpenTapePhraseRule rows: NO REWIND on a relative or indexed file is COBOL1802 and REVERSED on one is COBOL2210, at every edition that accepts the phrase, 85 included. The other part, a file "entirely contained on one reel/unit" (§1985:VII.4.2.4 GR2), cannot be broken on this implementation: a sequential file is one host file (SequentialConnector.Category is the non-reel/unit category), no multi-reel/unit file exists, and nothing refuses the phrases for a file named in a MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause, which part b permits. On such a file the phrases then act as the neighbouring rules say: NoRewindPhraseEffect ignores NO REWIND with I-O status 07 (§1985:VII.4.3.4 GR10) and ReversedPhraseEffect positions the file at its end (§1985:VII.4.3.4 GR11). Probed at --std 85: OPEN INPUT of a relative file and of an indexed file with REVERSED and with NO REWIND are each refused (COBOL2210, COBOL1802); on two sequential files named in one MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause, OPEN OUTPUT WITH NO REWIND answers 07 and the file is written, OPEN INPUT WITH NO REWIND reads the first record, and OPEN INPUT REVERSED answers 00 and delivers the records last to first. The witness opens a sequential file OUTPUT WITH NO REWIND, writes one record, and reads it back under OPEN INPUT REVERSED to the at end condition.

The inapplicable-medium ignore case is 1985 GR10's (now §2023:14.9.27.4 GR11), not this rule's.
